title: OPC 10030 ISA-95 Common Object Model — ISA-95 Base Information Model
establishes: ISA-95 sets out a role-based equipment hierarchy — enterprise, site, area, work centre, work unit, equipment module and control module — and records a person's qualifications alongside results.
why_included: The formal standard for how a factory is structured. The only source defining the levels of the plant, and the basis for keeping a place on a line separate from the machine in it.

title: ISA-88
establishes: A batch procedure is an ordered set of unit procedures, operations and phases; recipes are general, site, master or control, and carry a formula, equipment requirements and a procedure.
why_included: The standard for how batch recipes are structured. It establishes the four levels of a recipe and that a recipe names the equipment it needs.

title: ISA-88 (S88) Batch Control Standard
establishes: S88 separates what is to be done from how equipment is driven, with parameter limits, recipe hierarchy, and batch records under electronic-record rules.
why_included: A practitioner reading of ISA-88. It confirms that recipes and equipment are held apart in practice and that parameters carry limits.

title: ISA-88
establishes: The equipment model says what the plant can do and the recipe says what to do; a recipe asks for 'heat to 80 for 20 minutes' and a new product variant becomes a new recipe, not new code.
why_included: Shows the recipe and the method used across several products on one tank, and that the plant structure maps onto how maintenance records machines.

title: Batch Genealogy
establishes: Genealogy links every raw-material lot, intermediate, step, test, packaging operation and shipping unit; the bill of materials defines expected links and the batch record the links that actually occurred, including splits and merges.
why_included: The clearest source separating what a batch should have used from what it did use. Also the main source on splitting and merging lots.

title: MES Traceability and Genealogy
establishes: Manufacturers need to answer which raw-material lots went into a batch, which finished products were affected, which operators and equipment were involved, and whether checks were completed.
why_included: States the questions a plant is asked in plain terms. Several data requirements are those questions.

title: How to do batch tracking for manufacturing
establishes: Many manufacturers track some parts by serial number and bulk materials by batch; a blend of two lots must record both; returned stock keeps its batch identity and remaining shelf life.
why_included: The only source stating that serial and batch tracking are mixed within one operation.

title: What is a manufacturing execution system?
establishes: Food and beverage production systems manage recipes, formulation, lot traceability and allergen control.
why_included: A general reference placing recipes, formulation and allergen control together in food manufacturing.

title: FSMA Final Rule on Requirements for Additional Traceability Records for Certain Foods
establishes: Businesses handling listed foods must keep key data elements for critical tracking events and provide them to the FDA within 24 hours, and must share information with supply-chain partners.
why_included: The regulation setting the twenty-four-hour limit on traceability records. The primary legal source for recall.

title: FDA FSMA 204 Food Traceability Rule
establishes: The FDA has proposed extending the FSMA 204 compliance date to 20 July 2028; critical tracking events include packing, shipping and receiving.
why_included: Gives the current compliance date, which the model must be ready for.

title: FSMA 204 General Summary
establishes: A traceability lot code is assigned at initial packing or transformation, linked at each tracking event, exchanged between trading partners, and kept for two years; its source may be identified by registration number, location number or web address.
why_included: States when lot codes are assigned, how long they are kept, and that places are identified by several authorities.

title: Nonconformance: Definition, Types, Causes, and Process
establishes: A deviation is a departure from an approved procedure; a nonconformance is a failure to meet a requirement; nonconformances are classified minor, major or critical.
why_included: Draws the line between a departure from procedure and a failure against specification.

title: Deviation Management Process in GMP
establishes: Deviations are recorded, risk-classified and investigated, lead to corrective action, and support decisions about what to do with the batch.
why_included: Connects a departure from procedure to investigation, corrective action and the decision on the batch.

title: Non-conformance report
establishes: Affected material is contained, a disposition decided — use as is, rework, repair, scrap or return to supplier — with approvals, root cause found for significant or repeat issues, and closure verified.
why_included: Sets out the disposition choices and that each needs approval.

title: Deviation management
establishes: US GMP rule 21 CFR 211.192 requires a thorough investigation of any deviation, with conclusions and follow-up recorded.
why_included: The regulatory basis for investigating every departure from procedure.

title: MES and CMMS integration
establishes: The production system often knows a line stopped with a reason code while the maintenance system still shows the machine as available; connecting them makes one stoppage drive both.
why_included: The source for recording a stoppage once, seen by production and maintenance alike.

title: OEE data accuracy best practices
establishes: Downtime reasons must be standardised into tiers; when operators pick from many vague reasons, a changeover is logged four different ways.
why_included: Establishes that stoppage reasons must come from a governed list.

title: Food plant production uptime
establishes: Equipment effectiveness is availability times performance times quality; food plants start with structured failure codes on every stoppage and focus on their most critical machines.
why_included: Food-specific evidence on critical machines and failure recording.

title: ISO 22716 batch traceability
establishes: ISO 22716 requires documentation of every stage of cosmetic production from raw materials to distribution, and US cosmetics law now aligns with it on traceability.
why_included: Evidence that the traceability structures used in food also apply to cosmetics.

title: ISO 22716 and raw material management
establishes: Raw materials require supplier qualification, testing against specification, documented receipt, controlled storage, and batch tracking with deviation management.
why_included: The main source on qualifying suppliers and checking what arrives.

title: Guidance for Industry: Cosmetic Good Manufacturing Practices
establishes: Documentation should capture every aspect of manufacturing so that problems can be traced and corrected.
why_included: The US regulator's position on cosmetics records.

title: ISO 22716 — Cosmetics GMP
establishes: ISO 22716 covers personnel, premises, equipment and maintenance, materials, production, quality control, contract and outsourced activities, recalls and complaints, and expects any batch to be reconstructable.
why_included: The only source putting outside manufacturers under the same good-practice rules as own plants.

title: Turnkey vs. Tolling — Which Makes Sense for Me?
establishes: In tolling the brand supplies its own raw materials; in turnkey manufacturing the contract manufacturer provides them.
why_included: Defines the two arrangements. The scope settles on turnkey.

title: Contract Manufacturing Solutions
establishes: In turnkey contract manufacturing the manufacturer sources materials, makes, checks and packs the product; the client provides specifications and approvals.
why_included: States who does what in turnkey manufacturing.

title: California Cleaning Products Right to Know Act
establishes: Household cleaning manufacturers must disclose each ingredient, its CAS number, its function and a link to its safety data sheet; some may be withheld as confidential under a generic name.
why_included: The household-products regime for ingredient disclosure — a subgroup otherwise unsourced.

title: Cleansing Product Information Disclosure Program: Recommended Best Management Practices
organisation: New York State Department of Environmental Conservation
establishes: Manufacturers of household cleansing products furnish each ingredient and its content by weight; confidential business information may be withheld.
why_included: A second state regime confirming ingredient disclosure by weight for household products.

title: FSMA: legal ramifications of cGMPs are important to pet food safety
establishes: Facilities making animal food, including pet food, must comply with good manufacturing practice under 21 CFR Part 507.
why_included: The regulatory basis for pet food manufacturing — a subgroup otherwise unsourced.

title: Managing pet food ingredients
establishes: Pet food uses more than 500 ingredients; manufacturers identify hazards and put preventive controls such as heat treatment in place; the FDA regulates both finished pet food and its ingredients.
why_included: Evidence that pet food carries the same ingredient and control structures as human food.

title: Good pet food manufacturing practice
establishes: Responsible pet food makers run supplier approval, precise formulation, and batch records of finished product and where it went.
why_included: Industry-body evidence for supplier approval and batch records in pet food.

title: The GTIN management handbook
establishes: A change to declared formulation — such as adding nuts, which introduces an allergen — net content, a certification mark or pack quantity requires a new product number at every packing level.
why_included: The external rule for when a change makes a new product rather than a new version.

title: GTIN allocation rules
establishes: Formulation is the list of ingredients or components used to create a trade item; any change to the declared net content requires a new product number.
why_included: Confirms the same rule and defines formulation.

title: 21 CFR Part 11
establishes: Part 11 sets when electronic records and signatures are acceptable — identity, authority, auditability and retention — across food, cosmetics and other regulated manufacturing.
why_included: The regulatory basis for signatures and for never altering a recorded entry.

title: Electronic Batch Record
establishes: A batch record documents each step — by whom or by which equipment, when, with what materials and quantities, and with what results — including checks by a second qualified person.
why_included: Defines what a batch record must hold.

title: CPG Sec. 555.250 Statement of Policy for Labeling and Preventing Cross-contact of Common Food Allergens
establishes: Allergens must be declared; cross-contact arises from rework, carry-over on shared equipment and production sequencing.
why_included: The regulator's statement that the order products run in is a safety matter.

title: FDA Releases Draft Compliance Policy Guide for Major Food Allergen Labeling and Cross-contact
establishes: Nine major food allergens must be declared by the food they come from — whey must be declared as milk.
why_included: Establishes that an allergen is declared by its source, including when it arrives inside another ingredient.

title: FDA Issues Two Guidance Documents on Food Allergen Labeling Requirements
establishes: Food allergen labelling rules do not apply to pet foods, animal feeds, cosmetics, drugs or household cleaning products.
why_included: The only source stating that hazard declaration rules differ by subgroup.

title: GS1 2D code printing
establishes: A GS1 2D code carries the product number, batch, production date, expiry date and serial number; retailers are to accept 2D codes by the end of 2027.
why_included: Evidence that individual serial numbers are becoming readable on consumer packs.

title: GS1 Sunrise 2027
establishes: Sunrise 2027 is not a legal requirement, but major retailers are aligning to it, with packs carrying both codes during the transition.
why_included: Establishes that individual identification is expected commercially rather than required by law.

title: Guide to batch tracking
establishes: At receipt, capture supplier lot, quantity, expiry and certificate reference; record exact storage locations; issue lot-tracked materials to production orders.
why_included: The source for what is captured when material arrives and where it is kept.

title: Traceability — End-to-End Lot Genealogy
establishes: Traceability links identity (product number, lot, serial), status (quarantined, released) and events (receipt, consume, transform, pack, ship, return).
why_included: Establishes that stock carries a status such as quarantined or released, separate from its identity.
